title: 10% battery notification is not returning when the notebook's power cable is unplugged before reaching 11%
line: Unplugging the charger while the battery is still low now shows the low battery notification again.
explanation: PowerDevil only showed the low and critical battery notifications when the charge dropped across the threshold. Plugging in the charger closes the notification, and unplugging it again only showed "Running on Battery Power", so a battery that was still low gave no warning at all. The change checks the charge again when the charger is unplugged, with the same call already used after resume and unlock.

commits.message:
daemon: Warn about low battery again when the charger is unplugged

The low and critical battery notifications were only shown when the charge
crossed the threshold, so unplugging the charger while the battery was still
low showed nothing. Check the charge again on unplug, as after resume.

BUG: 500190

patches.diff:
From 1028e60e6d953a215a618d7386b8de85061b1b67 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:18:39 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] daemon: Warn about low battery again when the charger is
 unplugged

The low and critical battery notifications were only shown when the charge
crossed the threshold, so unplugging the charger while the battery was still
low showed nothing. Check the charge again on unplug, as after resume.

BUG: 500190
---
 daemon/powerdevilcore.cpp | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/daemon/powerdevilcore.cpp b/daemon/powerdevilcore.cpp
index 33badced8..1ec4486c8 100644
--- a/daemon/powerdevilcore.cpp
+++ b/daemon/powerdevilcore.cpp
@@ -736,6 +736,9 @@ void Core::onAcAdapterStateChanged(BatteryController::AcAdapterState state)
         m_powerCordUnpluggedNotification->setText(i18n("The power cord has been unplugged."));
 
         m_powerCordUnpluggedNotification->sendEvent();
+
+        // warn again if the battery is still low
+        emitBatteryChargePercentNotification(currentChargePercent(), 1000 /* so current is always lower than previous */);
     }
 }
 
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Battery at 8%, charger plugged in and unplugged again: no warning
Same steps: the Battery Low notification comes back

review.text: Re-invoking emitBatteryChargePercentNotification(currentChargePercent(), 1000) in Core::onAcAdapterStateChanged when transitioning to Unplugged cleanly fixes the missing low-battery warning on unplug. It matches the existing PowerDevil idiom used after startup, resume, and unlock, avoids duplicate notifications via handleLowBattery's existing guard, and handles critical battery levels consistently. Verification with dbusmock UPower covers low, normal, critical, and suspend/resume paths, and all unit tests pass.

reviews.text: Re-invoking emitBatteryChargePercentNotification(currentChargePercent(), 1000) in Core::onAcAdapterStateChanged when transitioning to Unplugged cleanly fixes the missing low-battery warning on unplug. It matches the existing PowerDevil idiom used after startup, resume, and unlock, avoids duplicate notifications via handleLowBattery's existing guard, and handles critical battery levels consistently. Verification with dbusmock UPower covers low, normal, critical, and suspend/resume paths, and all unit tests pass.

This matches Kai's diagnosis in c2 and the reporter's 6.7.5 reconfirmation (c4). Re-running the existing threshold check with previous=1000 on unplug is the same idiom already used for resume, unlock and session start, so it is minimal and in the right place, and handleLowBattery's guard prevents duplicates. The dbusmock before/after evidence, the 50% (no warning), 4% (critical) and sleep/resume checks are adequate. Nits: unplugging at or below the critical level now starts the 60 s critical action countdown, a behaviour change the MR text should mention. The side remark in c0 (unplug at 11%, no warning at 10%/9%) wasn't re-checked, though master's threshold-crossing logic should already handle it.
